criteria.name: Outbound prospecting
criteria.description: Starting conversations with new prospects: cold calls, cold emails, social selling, sequences.

anchors.0: No outbound or prospecting work mentioned.
anchors.1: Inbound-only sales or a generic claim of being a 'people person'.
anchors.2: Some outbound activity mentioned (calls or emails) without volume or results.
anchors.3: Regular outbound prospecting with stated channels and activity levels (e.g. 60 dials a day, multi-step email sequences).
anchors.4: Sustained, high-volume multi-channel prospecting with specifics: daily activity, meetings booked per month, and refined messaging or sequences.

criteria.name: Quota or target attainment
criteria.description: Meeting or beating sales, meeting or pipeline targets, shown with numbers.

anchors.1: Says targets were met, with no numbers.
anchors.2: One target result with a number but no context (period, size of target).
anchors.3: Quota or target attainment with numbers and period (e.g. 110% of meetings quota in Q2).
anchors.4: Consistent attainment over several periods with numbers, ranking or awards (e.g. top 3 of 20 reps, President's Club).

criteria.name: Lead research and qualification
criteria.description: Researching accounts, building lists and qualifying leads before passing them on.

anchors.0: No research or qualification work mentioned.
anchors.1: Generic claim of being 'organized' or 'detail-oriented' only.
anchors.2: Mentions building lead lists or qualifying leads, without a method.
anchors.3: Describes a qualification method or research process (e.g. BANT, ideal customer profile, account research before calls).
anchors.4: Clear, repeatable research and qualification practice with results (e.g. improved conversion from meeting to opportunity, built territory plans).

criteria.name: Objection handling and communication
criteria.description: Handling objections and communicating value clearly by phone and in writing.

anchors.0: No persuasive communication or objection handling mentioned.
anchors.1: Generic claim of strong communication only.
anchors.2: Mentions handling objections or pitching, without examples.
anchors.3: Describes handling common objections or delivering pitches, with an approach or outcome.
anchors.4: Specific, repeated examples of turning objections into meetings or deals, or writing scripts and training others.

criteria.name: Sales tools
criteria.description: CRMs and sales engagement platforms used in prospecting work.

anchors.1: General office or computer skills only.
anchors.2: One CRM or sales tool named without how it was used.
anchors.3: One or more CRM or sales engagement tools named with how they were used (e.g. logging activity in Salesforce, running Outreach sequences).
anchors.4: Several sales tools used in depth: building sequences, reports or dashboards, list enrichment, or training others.

criteria.name: B2B or industry knowledge
criteria.description: Experience selling to businesses, ideally software or services.

anchors.1: Consumer sales only, with no business customers described.
anchors.2: Some business customers or a related industry, with little detail.
anchors.3: Sold to businesses, with buyer types or industry named (e.g. SMB SaaS, IT managers).
anchors.4: Deep B2B knowledge: multiple buyer personas, complex sales cycles, or a clear industry specialism.

nice_to_haves.name: Social selling
nice_to_haves.description: Uses LinkedIn or other social channels to prospect.

nice_to_haves.name: CRM hygiene
nice_to_haves.description: Keeps CRM data accurate: logging, stage updates, notes.
